title: Lazur vs MacWhisper on Mac in 2026: live voice help or on-device file transcription
metaTitle: Lazur vs MacWhisper for Mac: voice help or file transcription
description: Lazur vs MacWhisper on Mac: file transcription on your device, or a voice assistant that sees your screen. Prices and features from each site.
intro: MacWhisper is the better pick if you want to turn recordings, meetings and video files into text on your Mac. Lazur is the better pick if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, answers out loud and points at things. Both can dictate, so the real question is what you need help with.
tldr: MacWhisper transcribes files, video, URLs and meetings on your Mac. It also dictates.
Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen. It also dictates into any app.
Pick MacWhisper for recordings, subtitles and transcripts that can stay on your Mac.
Pick Lazur for on-screen help, pointing and step-by-step guidance.
Lazur Pro is $18/month after a 3-day trial. MacWhisper's homepage lists Pro at €64, one-time.

blocks.text: Lazur vs MacWhisper: what each app does

MacWhisper is a transcription app first. You drop in an audio or video file, and it turns the speech into text on your Mac. You can export that text as subtitles or a document. Lazur is a voice assistant first. You hold a key, ask a question, and it answers out loud while it looks at your screen. Both apps can type your speech into another app, but that overlap is the smaller part of each product.

A quick test helps. Ask what you need this week. If the answer is a folder of interviews or a meeting you missed, you need a transcription tool. If the answer is a settings screen you cannot find, you need an assistant that can see that screen. Most people hit one of those problems more often than the other, and that is usually enough to decide.
Where MacWhisper is the better pick for files and meetings

MacWhisper handles recordings you already have. Drag a file onto the window, or paste a link to a media file, and it transcribes it. The homepage also lists batch processing, so you can queue several files at once. Say you have a folder with twelve lecture recordings. You queue them and come back when the work is done. That is the job MacWhisper is built for.

Export is the other strength. The homepage lists .srt, .vtt, plain text, .pdf, .docx, .md and .html. Subtitles for a video need .srt or .vtt. A client memo may need .docx. Notes for a wiki may suit .md. Speaker recognition and filler-word removal clean up the result, so you spend less time editing. The homepage says it covers 100+ languages.

items: Batch transcription of audio and video files
Subtitles in .srt or .vtt for a video you publish
Recording an online meeting or the audio from one app
Keeping transcription on your Mac with local models

blocks.text: Is MacWhisper private? What on-device transcription means

MacWhisper's homepage says it uses local models to transcribe files, and that sensitive content can be processed without data leaving your Mac. Its privacy policy, dated 14 March 2024, says no audio, text or other data leaves your device. The same policy says the app can send anonymous analytics events about licensing status. That is the core promise, and it matters for private interviews and client recordings.

The fine print matters. AI features such as summaries and chat can use cloud models. Cloud transcription, translation and AI services are opt-in, and they send data to the provider you choose. The App Store listing says the same thing in plain words: audio or transcript text goes off your Mac only when you choose a cloud service. So the rule is simple. Local models keep the work on your Mac. A cloud model sends it out.
Check the cloud switch before you run client work

Open the feature you plan to use, and check which model and provider it runs. A transcript made with a local model stays on your Mac. A summary sent to a cloud chat model does not. The common mistake is assuming every AI feature is local because the transcription is. Test each step on a file you do not mind sharing, so you know exactly what leaves the Mac.
Where Lazur is the better pick for help with your screen

Lazur is built for the work in front of you. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do a task, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on. It does not click for you. It does not edit files or operate other apps either.

Here is a worked example. You open an app you have never used, and you cannot find the export option. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where export is. Lazur points at the spot. You click it. Then you ask for the next step. The task stays in your hands, and you learn the app as you go. MacWhisper's homepage does not describe this kind of help. Its pages cover files, meetings and dictation.

items: You get stuck in apps and want someone to point at the button.
You want to ask what a word, an error or a chart on screen means.
You want timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events and music by voice.
You want web research run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, with a summary and a report.

blocks.text: Lazur also remembers what you asked and did, and it keeps that memory on the Mac. Background research runs through the Lazur for Chrome extension and comes back as a summary and a report. MacWhisper's homepage lists neither of these. Pick Lazur when your problem is the next click, not the last recording.
Dictation in Lazur and MacWhisper

Both apps dictate into other apps, so this is where people compare them most. MacWhisper's homepage lists system-wide dictation with automatic grammar improvement and filler-word removal. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at the cursor when you hold fn. It adds snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots, so the words you use often are easier to get right.

Dictation is not MacWhisper's headline. Voibe, a competing dictation app that discloses its role in the comparison, scores MacWhisper 5/10 for real-time dictation. The same reviewer calls MacWhisper a superb transcription app, just not a dictation-first one. Treat that as one reviewer's opinion. It does line up with the product, which is built around files.

Dictation is also not Lazur's headline. Lazur says dictation is included and is not the main feature. If you dictate all day, test both apps on your own text. Dictate the same email in each app, then compare the errors you fix afterward. That test tells you more than any score from me or from a reviewer.
Lazur vs MacWhisper prices: $18 a month or €64 once

Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. After the trial, Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually. Pro includes 250 AI actions and Power includes 1,000. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

MacWhisper's homepage lists a free tier at €0 per month, free forever. It lists Pro at €64 per license, with a one-time payment and lifetime updates. The MacWhisper /pricing page returned a 404 when I checked, so the homepage is the source here. I could not open the Gumroad checkout to confirm the price. One third-party site, WhipScribe, reported €65 at checkout on 26 October 2026. That conflicts with €64, so check the Gumroad page before you buy.

The App Store version, Whisper Transcription, uses a different price list. Its App Store page shows Pro Lifetime at $99.99 and an Assistant subscription at $9.99 a month. The currencies differ across these pages, so do not compare the sums directly. Convert on the day you buy. Twelve monthly payments of $18 come to $216 a year. Annual billing at $15 a month comes to $180.

A single MacWhisper license has no monthly charge. If you only want transcription, that is the simpler shape of price. If you want the assistant, the monthly price is what you pay for. Lazur's price covers a different job from MacWhisper's, so the real question is which job you will use every week.
Mistakes people make when they choose

items: Buying the App Store version and expecting a license key. Its docs say the App Store build does not accept license keys.
Expecting Lazur to transcribe a folder of recordings. Its listed features are live talk and dictation.
Expecting MacWhisper to point at buttons. Its homepage covers files, meetings and dictation, not on-screen guidance.
Running a large model on a Mac with 8 GB of RAM. WhipScribe says the Medium and Large models need more than 8 GB.

blocks.text: Which Mac does each app need?

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. MacWhisper is macOS only. The App Store build, Whisper Transcription, requires macOS 15.0 or later. I could not confirm the minimum for the direct build from the developer's own pages. One secondary source says macOS 14.0 or later, but I could not verify it. Check the download page before you install.

RAM matters for MacWhisper's larger models. WhipScribe says the Medium and Large models need more than 8 GB of RAM. If your Mac has 8 GB, start with a smaller model and time one file. Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers while you hold the key, so it depends on a connection to answer you.
A worked week: which app saves more time

Take a typical week with a few recordings, a couple of meetings and a lot of email. MacWhisper turns the recordings into text in one batch, and you export only the files you need. Lazur does not transcribe those files, so the recordings need a transcription tool. For the meetings, MacWhisper can record the call itself, which Lazur does not list as a feature.

Now the screen work. Each time you reach a settings page you do not know, Lazur can answer with a pointer. Those small stops add up. They can cost more time than a recording does, especially when you switch between new apps. Track the stops for one day. Note which ones were about files and which were about screens. That count shows which app earns its place.
Which one should you try first?

Start with the work you do most often. If that work is recordings, start with MacWhisper's free tier and transcribe a file you already have. If it is questions about apps and screens, start Lazur's 3-day trial and ask it about a screen you find confusing. Both tests take one afternoon.

items: Write down the last three tasks where you were stuck or typing for a long time.
If most are files or meetings, install MacWhisper and run one real recording.
If most are on-screen help or app questions, download Lazur and start the trial.
If you need both, test each one on your own work before you pay for either.

blocks.text: You can [download Lazur](/download) or check the [current plans](/pricing) on the Lazur site. Looking for other transcription options? See the [MacWhisper alternatives](/alternatives/macwhisper) page. For a dictation app with a different angle, read [Lazur vs Superwhisper](/compare/lazur-vs-super-whisper).
Can you use Lazur and MacWhisper together?

Yes. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. MacWhisper's dictation has its own shortcut, which you set in its settings. Check it, and change one of the two if they clash. Running both is simple once the shortcuts do not overlap.
Want numbers for your own typing? Try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).

faq.question: Is Lazur a good MacWhisper alternative?
faq.answer: Only if you want more than transcription. Lazur dictates in any Mac app, and it also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you one click at a time. If you mainly transcribe files and meetings, MacWhisper is the better fit.

faq.question: Can Lazur transcribe audio or video files?
faq.answer: Lazur's listed features are live. You hold a key and talk, or hold fn to dictate. Its feature list does not include transcribing files, so use MacWhisper for recordings, video and media URLs.

faq.question: Does MacWhisper keep my audio on my Mac?
faq.answer: With local models, the developer's privacy policy dated 14 March 2024 says no audio, text or other data leaves your device, apart from anonymous licensing analytics. Cloud transcription, translation and AI features are opt-in and send data to the provider you choose.

faq.question: Is MacWhisper cheaper than Lazur?
faq.answer: It depends on how long you use it. MacWhisper's homepage lists Pro at €64 once. Lazur Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually. The currencies differ, so convert on the day you buy.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and MacWhisper together?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Check MacWhisper's dictation shortcut in its settings, and change one of them if the two clash.

verdict: Pick MacWhisper if you transcribe recordings, meetings or video and want that work to stay on your Mac. Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, points at buttons and talks you through apps. If you have both kinds of work, you could use both, but test each one on your own tasks first.
